claim_ceiling: A PASS establishes only synthetic task-event contract integrity and expected disposition for the exact corpus. It does not establish human performance, safe takeover, navigation competence, seaworthiness, certification or authority to operate.

cases.description: Complete current packet and scoped on-time acknowledgement permit a bounded transfer.
Operator declines; the declared local contingency continues without a handover.
No situation packet is available; the operator cannot accept an informed transfer.
A stale packet cannot support a new transfer.
Contradictory ownship position/time sources require clarification, not a confident transfer.
Situation packet belongs to a superseded vessel configuration.
A packet contains simulator-only oracle state and is inadmissible for deployment mode.
AIS-only target report cannot be relabelled as local sensor truth.
Derived target views lack source lineage and cannot count as independent corroboration.
Transfer authority expired before the operator acknowledgement.
The logged-in role lacks the exact vessel/function authority scope.
Authority is revoked after acceptance but before lease grant.
No acknowledgement arrives before the declared deadline; local fallback continues.
Acknowledgement after the deadline cannot retroactively authorize transfer.
Operator accepted but the transfer response is lost; outcome requires reconciliation, not duplicate command.
Declared remote operator is unavailable; no transfer is accepted.
Operator is declared occupied by a concurrent incident; transfer requires fallback or reassignment.
Communications fail before transfer acknowledgement; local fallback remains active.
Duplicate acknowledgement with same transaction ID must not create a second authority grant.
Repeated/duplicated alerts for one incident must not fragment or reset the handover transaction.
Displayed autonomy mode disagrees with the source-bound function allocation.
Operator receives a packet showing a local contingency already executing and does not restart or cancel it blindly.
Required local contingency is unknown; evaluator must not invent one or claim successful safe handover.
After recovery, fresh checks and a valid approval permit a scoped return to bounded autonomy.
Prior approval is stale; re-entry to higher autonomy is blocked.
Vessel software/configuration changed after the evidence and approval were issued.
A future-dated observation is rejected and cannot be used for current mode transfer.
UTC and monotonic clock mappings conflict beyond their declared tolerance.
Transport duplication of idempotent packet-delivery events leaves the final disposition unchanged.
Non-semantic field order/presentation changes do not change source roles or transfer disposition.
Packet arrives only after the handover deadline; no stale request can be revived.
Two overlapping command leases are proposed; the second grant is rejected.
A key target track has no admitted source receipt, so the packet is incomplete.
